_comment: Curated Ollama models for agent use. size_gb = download/disk size shown on ollama.com/library (decimal GB, checked 2026-10). kv_gb_32k = estimated KV-cache memory at a 32K context (fp16), computed from each model's published architecture; once a model is downloaded the panel computes the exact value from the model itself. 'tools' is what Ollama's library advertises (the model was trained/templated for function calling in general) - this is NOT the same as 'openclaw_tool_calling' below, which is specifically about whether OpenClaw's own agent harness can successfully drive that model's tool calls end to end. Edit freely.
_openclaw_tool_calling_values: verified_working (tested here: the agent reliably invokes a real file/shell tool and the task completes) | verified_broken (tested here: it does not, see the model's note for what was observed) | untested (no data yet - this is most of the list)

models.name: qwen3:1.7b
models.note: Tiny; fast on almost anything, but weak at multi-step agent work. Tool calling tested broken here (2026-10): instead of invoking a tool, it prints the tool-call JSON as plain reply text.

models.name: llama3.2:3b
models.note: Small and quick; fine for simple tasks.

models.name: phi4-mini:3.8b
models.note: Small, supports function calling in general; not verified through OpenClaw specifically.

models.name: qwen3:4b
models.note: Good small all-rounder for laptops and CPU-only machines.

models.name: qwen2.5:7b
models.note: Older generation; very light on memory for its size.

models.name: llama3.1:8b
models.note: Solid general model with tool calling in general; not verified through OpenClaw specifically.

models.name: qwen3:8b
models.note: Recommended for 8-12 GB GPUs or 16 GB Macs. Same Qwen3 tool-call template as the 1.7B/14B sizes that tested broken here, so treat with suspicion until verified.

models.name: qwen2.5:14b
models.note: Older generation of the 14B class. A different tool-call template from Qwen3, so the Qwen3 failure found here may not apply - genuinely untested, not a guess.

models.name: qwen3:14b
models.note: The default here, and a strong chat model. But tool calling tested broken through OpenClaw (2026-10): the agent describes using a tool in plain text instead of invoking it, or emits a malformed call OpenClaw's harness rejects. Tried a larger context window (up to the model's own 40960 maximum) and OpenClaw compat flags (supportsTools, thinkingFormat); neither changed the outcome. Fine for plain chat, not yet usable for the VM-bench 'agent does the task' feature.

models.name: gpt-oss:20b
models.note: OpenAI's open-weight reasoning model; strong but heavy. Uses its own tool-call format (harmony), different from Qwen3's - worth trying if you want to test another local model for the VM-bench feature.

models.name: qwen3:30b
models.note: Mixture-of-experts: needs lots of memory but runs fast. 24 GB+ GPU or 48 GB+ unified memory. Same Qwen3 family as the two sizes that tested broken here.

models.name: qwen3:32b
models.note: Strongest local option here; 32 GB+ GPU memory or 64 GB Mac. Same Qwen3 family as the two sizes that tested broken here.
